---
title: "Async/Await: A Future Is Not a Thread"
description: "One Rust language concept taught with one short runnable example and a precise explanation."
---

## The question

**Does calling an `async fn` immediately perform its body?**

Calling an async function creates a **Future**. That future must be polled by an executor to make progress. `async` is not equivalent to `thread::spawn`, and the standard library doesn't supply a general-purpose executor API like Tokio.

## The rule to remember

First understand the Future model; add a runtime only when the task actually needs asynchronous I/O.

## The smallest complete example

Paste into `main.rs` and run with `rustc --edition 2024 main.rs && ./main`. The [Rust examples page](examples/index.qmd) describes how to check all snippets automatically.

~~~rust
async fn answer() -> u8 {
    7
}
fn main() {
    let _future = answer(); // created, not executed
    println!("a future was created");
}
~~~

**Follow the state:** The program prints only the message from `main`. The future has not been polled, so the `answer` body has not run. For real network I/O, choose an async runtime and await the future.

## Important limitation

An `async` operation can still block an executor if it calls a blocking synchronous operation. Async is about cooperative progress at suspension points, not automatically parallel CPU execution.
